transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I'm a construction manager, and I'm here because I'm having a really hard time staying focused at work. In long meetings and even out on the site, my mind just keeps drifting, and I can't seem to track what people are saying or what I'm supposed to be keeping tabs on. It's starting to cause some really serious problems with my projects, so I figured it was time to get some help.
Have you struggled with these attention and focus issues since you were a child, or is this a relatively new problem that started more recently?

It's gotten a lot worse over the last two years since I took on much bigger construction projects, but the truth is it goes all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, teachers were constantly sending notes home about me daydreaming, talking over other kids, and never finishing my worksheets unless someone stood right over me.
Aside from the focus issues, have you been experiencing persistent, excessive worry about work or other areas of your life, along with feeling constantly on edge or tense?

I wouldn't say I have persistent, excessive worry or feel constantly tense on a normal basis. I definitely get stressed and frustrated when I make mistakes at work or lose track of things, but it's really just a direct reaction to those focus issues.
Over the past few weeks or months, have you been feeling consistently down, sad, or hopeless, or have you lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?

No, I haven't really been feeling down, sad, or hopeless, and I haven't lost interest in my usual activities. I do feel incredibly stressed and frustrated about my current struggles at work, but it's more about the situation itself rather than feeling depressed.
Do you often feel restless, find it hard to sit still, or tend to act impulsively in your daily life, both now and when you were younger?

Yes, absolutely—during long meetings I can't stay in my chair and constantly have to get up, and waiting my turn makes me feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. I also act impulsively by blurting out answers and interrupting people mid-sentence. This goes right back to my childhood, when my teachers would send notes home about me talking over other kids in class.

The candidate remains F90.0 and we can finalize the diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a clear, chronic pattern of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity originating in childhood (elementary school) and persisting into adulthood. These symptoms cause significant functional impairment in his occupational role as a construction manager. Differential diagnoses such as generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) and depressive disorders (F32.9) were evaluated and ruled out, as the patient's stress and frustration are situational and directly secondary to his executive dysfunction.
